fix.notes: The preaggregation tables are fully rebuilt on each run so no migration script is required. The change is limited to schema precision only; query logic is unchanged. No other issues found in the area.
fix.pr_body:
## What was wrong

The four preaggregation tables in `decksite/data/playability.py` stored `playability` as `DECIMAL(6,5)`, giving only 5 decimal places and a minimum representable non-zero value of 0.00001 (1-in-100,000). Cards played in fewer than 1 in 100,000 decks would round to exactly 0.00000, making them indistinguishable from completely unplayed cards. The practical threshold discussed in issue #12331 is around 1-in-200,000 (0.000005), which is already below the old precision limit.

## What changed

All four `playability DECIMAL(6,5)` column definitions in the four preaggregation table `CREATE TABLE` statements were changed to `DECIMAL(10,9)`, giving 9 decimal places and a minimum non-zero value of 0.000000001 — well below any realistic playability threshold. These tables are preaggregates rebuilt on every run, so no manual migration is needed.

Files changed: `decksite/data/playability.py` (4 lines changed)

## Validation

- `uv run --frozen python dev.py lint` — passed
- `uv run --frozen python dev.py unit` — 845 passed, 1 skipped (18s)

Fixes #12331
fix.pr_title: Increase playability column precision from DECIMAL(6,5) to DECIMAL(10,9) (#12331)
